question: Does a gradient-informed diagonal metric estimator, as a research flag in the warmup, raise ESS per gradient on the house posteriordb models without losing gates?
motivation: WP58 (STUDIES/nutpie_per_gradient_gap_v1): of the pooled per-gradient gap to nutpie, the mass matrix accounts for 44 % (Python path) / 60 % (Rust path) and warmup cost for 44 %; nutpie estimates the diagonal from draw and gradient variances, sigma_i^2 = sqrt(var(x_i) / var(g_i)). In v7 nutpie led oWALNUTS per gradient most on the regressions (sblrc 2.82x, kidiq 1.63x, earnings 1.47x, nes2000 1.37x) and the autoregressions (arma11 2.19x, arK 1.31x).
library_under_test: wt/gradient-metric: main 70e4c958 plus library commit 5cfbd199. One research flag, off by default: walnutpie::DiagonalMetricEstimator {DrawVariance (default), GradientInformed, GradientInformedOverlap} as WarmupConfig::diagonal_metric_estimator (builder with_diagonal_metric_estimator behind the existing `research` Cargo feature); src/walnutpie.rs only, plus tests/gradient_metric.rs. With the default estimator no gradient statistics are accumulated (the gradient accumulator is None) and the warmup code path is the shipped one.

estimator.inputs: per chain, over each slow warmup window (the transitions at which the shipped estimator updates its Welford accumulator): the selected position x (the chain state after the transition) and the log-density gradient g at that same state (the selected state's cached gradient; no extra target evaluations). Both accumulated with Welford's algorithm (count n, mean, m2) in the unconstrained coordinates.
estimator.per_coordinate: var_x_i = m2_x_i / (n - 1), var_g_i = m2_g_i / (n - 1); s_i = sqrt(var_x_i / var_g_i) when var_x_i and var_g_i are finite and > 0 and the ratio is finite and > 0; otherwise s_i = var_x_i (the shipped draw variance).
estimator.regularisation: the configured DiagonalMetricRegularization applied to s_i with the window count n; in every arm here that is DEFAULT_METRIC_REGULARIZATION = Stan: v_i = (n / (n + 5)) * s_i + 1e-3 * (5 / (n + 5)); then floored at MIN_ADAPTATION_VARIANCE and inverted to the mass (the API's convention), exactly as the shipped rule treats the draw variance.
estimator.installation: unchanged: at the end of each slow window the new diagonal is installed, the dual-averaging stream restarts (no initial step search in the sampler default), and the accumulators are reset. No update when n < 2 (as shipped).
estimator.GradientInformed: primary arm `gradmetric`: statistics of the current slow window only (the shipped window semantics).
estimator.GradientInformedOverlap: secondary arm `gradmetric-overlap`: the exact Chan merge of the previous slow window's and the current window's (x, g) statistics, n = merged count; the first slow window uses its own statistics. Consecutive estimates therefore overlap by one window (nutpie-style overlapping windows within the Stan schedule).
estimator.not_changed: window schedule, step adaptation, kernel, retained transitions, start rule. nutpie's own warmup schedule and its first-window 1/|g| initialisation are NOT transplanted: this study isolates the estimator.

window_schedule: WarmupWindowConfig::default() (Stan: initial fast buffer 75, base slow window 25 doubling, terminal fast buffer 50). At 1,000 warmup the slow windows are 25, 50, 100, 200, 500 transitions (transitions 75-924); at 2,000 warmup: 25, 50, 100, 200, 400, 1,100 (75-1,949). Recorded per chain in every cell (metric_updates).
machine: AWS EC2 c7a.4xlarge owalnuts-bench, lane 3: every build and cell under taskset -c 8-11, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1; files under ~/lanes/gradient_metric_v1/ only; other lanes active (shared L3 and memory bandwidth), so walls are 'pinned, co-tenanted' and are not used in any rule; ESS per gradient, pass counts and divergence counts are unaffected.
dispatch: posteriordb cells load owalnuts_bridgestan::ReplicatedStanTarget with 4 replicas (the WP65-qualified Linux concurrent-replica dispatch, execution ReplicatedConcurrent, recorded per cell).

arms.default: Sampler::new() defaults: Adaptation::default() (dual averaging 0.8 with DEFAULT_WARMUP_EXHAUSTION, DEFAULT_METRIC_REGULARIZATION = Stan, DEFAULT_CHAIN_RESCUE = None)
arms.gradmetric: Adaptation::Custom(WarmupConfig::new(0.8).with_warmup_exhaustion_rule(DEFAULT_WARMUP_EXHAUSTION).with_metric_regularization(DEFAULT_METRIC_REGULARIZATION).with_diagonal_metric_estimator(GradientInformed)); everything else default. With DrawVariance in place of GradientInformed this configuration is bit-identical to the default (tests/gradient_metric.rs).
arms.gradmetric-overlap: as gradmetric with GradientInformedOverlap (secondary; reported against the same rules, decides nothing)
arms.build: one harness build for all arms: owalnuts with the `research` feature (needed for the builder). The pipeline check compares the default arm's draws hash against a plain-feature build on one cell.

predicted_gainers_note: the correlated linear regressions where nutpie led oWALNUTS by >= 1.3x per gradient in v7. For a Gaussian posterior with covariance S, sqrt(var(x_i)/var(g_i)) = sqrt(S_ii / (S^-1)_ii), the geometric mean of the marginal and conditional variances, which shortens the trajectories forced by strongly correlated coefficients.

posteriordb.reader: files read directly (posteriors/*.json, models/stan/*.stan, data/data/*.json.zip, reference_posteriors/draws/draws/*.json.zip); no posteriordb package

bridgestan: BridgeStan 2.9.0 source (GitHub release tarball, sha256 b6034f83fb2ffb71ce7be9525b7dded1a225e9a4eaf4b75d4c7e97e3ade05a4c) in the lane directory; models compiled with its makefile defaults, make -j2 per model; Python bridgestan 2.9.0 from ~/venv (read-only) for param_constrain; ArviZ 0.23.4 from ~/venv for the statistics.
seed_check: git grep -nowE over every tracked file of 70e4c958 for 7174(0[1-9]|10) and 71750[1-3]: no hit (the neighbouring ranges 7101xx and 7171xx/7173xx have hits and were not used); no hit in any protocol.json / PREREGISTRATION.md of C:/dev/owalnuts-wt/*/STUDIES; the box lanes are checked before the first cell (recorded in environment.json). Pipeline seed 990671: no hit.
run_order: P (models in house order; within a model seeds ascending; within a seed default, gradmetric, gradmetric-overlap), then F (seeds ascending; within a seed the same arm order). One process per cell, strictly sequential, four threads. Cell timeout 2,700 s (v7). An errored or timed-out cell is a failed cell (posteriordb: not passed, and the model leaves that candidate's geomean per v7's rule; funnel: recorded as an error and excluded from the pooled estimate, which then has fewer seeds). Never rerun; a host-killed driver is a recorded deviation.
posteriordb_harness: STUDIES/refinement_levels10_v1/src/bin/pdb.rs (WP68 = v7/WP62 oWALNUTS cell) with the adaptation arms in place of the build arms and per-chain metric-update telemetry. Sampler::new() with only the run shape and admit_worst_case (plus the arm's adaptation); Init::default() (best_of(16)) starts drawn as the sampler would. Driver metrics are v7's: draws constrained through BridgeStan with transformed parameters, gate parameters = posteriordb reference-draw columns, ArviZ 0.23.4 rank R-hat, bulk ESS, tail ESS (0.05, 0.95), mean MCSE; gradients = target calls including start search, warmup and sampling.
funnel_harness: STUDIES/refinement_levels10_v1/src/bin/funnel.rs (WP68 = WP66 / WP53 harness) with the adaptation arms. Neal's 10-D funnel, house starts omega in {-3,-1,1,3}, x = 0, Metric::diagonal(), Tuning::default(), Limits::new().admit_worst_case(), 4 chains, 4 threads; statistic P(omega < -5), exact 0.0477903522728147.

statistics.posteriordb: per arm pass counts out of 51; per model the median over the 3 seeds of min bulk ESS per gradient; per candidate the ratio candidate / default per model and the geomean over the models whose 3 seeds are status ok on both arms (v7 rule); per model retained divergences summed over the 3 seeds.
statistics.warmup_gradient_share: per arm and per model: sum of warmup target calls (all four chains) / total target calls (start search + warmup + sampling), pooled over the arm's ok cells; reported before (default) and after (gradmetric, gradmetric-overlap), also per model. Descriptive, plus predictions Pc/Pd.
statistics.funnel: per arm: pooled P5 = mean of the 10 per-seed estimates, between-seed s.e. = sd / sqrt(10); retained divergences, exhaustions, median omega tail ESS, warmup gradient share, final mass of omega and x.

decision_rules.R1: posteriordb: geomean over models of (median ESS/gradient gradmetric) / (median ESS/gradient default) >= 1.10.
decision_rules.R2: posteriordb: gradmetric pass count >= default pass count (out of 51, v7 gates).
decision_rules.R3: posteriordb: 0 new divergences: for every model, gradmetric retained divergences summed over its 3 seeds <= default's.
decision_rules.F: funnel sanity arm: |pooled P5(gradmetric) - 0.0477903522728147| <= 1 x its between-seed s.e. (the coordinator's rule; a correct sampler fails it about 32 % of the time, recorded as a known property, not softened).
decision_rules.D: flag-off integrity on the box: git diff 70e4c958 of src/, tests/, Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock at the repository root touches only src/walnutpie.rs and tests/gradient_metric.rs; cargo test --release --test kernel_fingerprint passes without and with the research feature; tests/gradient_metric.rs passes (it includes the flag-off bit-identity test at the RunConfig and Sampler levels).
decision_rules.verdict: SUPPORTED iff R1, R2, R3, F and D hold for gradmetric; otherwise NOT SUPPORTED, naming the failed clauses. In either case the flag stays research-only and off by default (no default flip in this study). gradmetric-overlap is evaluated against the same rules and reported; it decides nothing.

predictions.R1-R3: the coordinator's predictions: geomean >= 1.10, pass count not lower, 0 new divergences
predictions.Pa: the predicted gainers (sblrc, kidiq, earnings, nes2000) have a higher geomean ratio than the other 13 models
predictions.Pb: at least 3 of the 4 predicted gainers are among the 6 models with the largest gradmetric / default ratio
predictions.Pc: the pooled warmup gradient share is lower with gradmetric than with default
predictions.Pd: the pooled warmup gradient share changes by less than 5 percentage points (most of WP58's warmup-cost gap is the schedule, not the estimator)
predictions.Pe: the gradmetric-overlap geomean ratio is within 5 % of the gradmetric ratio
predictions.Pf: any model that loses passes under gradmetric is gp_pois_regr or lotka_volterra (where WP58's nutpie-metric transplant lost gates)
predictions.Pg: funnel: gradmetric retained divergences <= default's (descriptive; the default arm runs 10 seeds as the reference)

pre_freeze_runs: Non-evidence, disclosed: three local Windows smoke runs of the funnel harness, all gradmetric on seed 990671: 1,000/2,000 and 2,000/2,000 (wall 0.1 s each, to confirm the slow windows 25/50/100/200/500 and 25/50/100/200/400/1,100) and one 2,000/20,000 cell through run_study.py with the artifacts redirected to a scratch directory (to exercise the driver and analysis; P5 0.0424, 0 divergences); on the box, the BridgeStan compile of the 17 models (infrastructure) and pipeline checks on seed 990671 (one eight_schools_noncentered posteriordb cell per arm, plus the default arm from a plain-feature build to compare draws hashes; one funnel cell per arm at 2,000/20,000) after these predictions were written; outputs in the lane scratch directory, not committed.
